intent: Bring the display and usb_query test modules under the 250-line cap, and remove the re-export block in display.py that the earlier partial split left behind.
scope: Non-goal: no assertion changed, no test deleted, skipped or weakened
changes: test_display.py split at TestClassifyPercentageLevel: the USB report tests stay, the consumable supply maths and its display go to test_supply_levels.py, which imports the six classification helpers from _supply directly and the two printing functions from display.

That was the last reader of the six _supply names through display, so display.py's __all__ shrank to the two public entry points, its _supply import narrowed to the one name it actually calls, and the stale comment claiming the tests reach those names through this module was deleted. Confirmed by grep across python_pkg that no source module or test still imports them from display.

test_usb_query.py split at TestRetryPjlQuery: discovery and PJL response parsing stay, the retry, sequencing, result init and query_usb_pjl tests go to test_usb_query_sequence.py. Those patch the wire helpers on usb_query rather than _pjl_io, which is correct - that is the module whose globals the sequencing code resolves them through.
Renamed test_usb_query_part2.py to test_pjl_io.py, matching the module it has covered since the source split.

verification.evidence: 402 passed before the split and 402 passed after it - identical pass count.

verification.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest python_pkg/brother_printer/tests -q (first run after the usb_query split)
verification.evidence: Reported 9 failed, 393 passed: TestParsePagecount sat between the two moved classes and travelled with them, so the new module needed errno, os, _parse_status and _parse_pagecount that my hand-written import block had not anticipated. Added; the count returned to 402.

verification.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c "from python_pkg.brother_printer import display as d; d._display_report_header; d._display_supply_levels; d._display_supply_warnings; d._display_network_device_info; d._display_page_count_estimate; d.display_cups_queue_status; d.get_status_info"
verification.evidence: runtime probe OK after the __all__ removal - every name the two display test modules patch is still a real attribute, so shrinking the re-export did not expose them to ruff's F401/TC001 rewrite.

Only check_brother_printer.py, test_display.py, test_display_part2.py and test_supply_levels.py import from display, and none of them names a _supply helper - which is what made the __all__ entries safe to drop rather than merely unused-looking.

verification.command: pre-commit run --files <the touched files and artifacts>
verification.evidence: ruff removed two imports the split left unused in test_usb_query.py; clean on re-run, and pytest-with-coverage passes.

risks: Removing names from __all__ is the one edit here that could break a caller silently at import time rather than loudly. Guarded by the repo-wide grep and the attribute probe, not by the test run alone.

test_usb_query_sequence.py patches _drain_buffer and pjl_query on usb_query while test_pjl_io.py patches their definitions on _pjl_io. Both are correct and must stay that way; collapsing them onto one module would unpatch the other caller.
rollback: git revert the commit; the two originals return at 363 and 328 lines, display.py's __all__ comes back, and the two new modules disappear.
After rollback, re-run the package suite and confirm it still reports 402 passed.
